comparator.name: Bestuurs- en organisatiewetenschap (Public Administration and Organisation Science)
comparator.sourceNotes: The student curriculum lists 180 EC: 142.5 EC in the major and 37.5 EC of profiling. The second-year 7.5 EC elective is part of profiling, alongside 30 EC in year three. The current graduation page cites a formal international study requirement. The publicly linked 2025–2026 regulation describes that requirement and course prerequisites for its own year, but lists a different first-year curriculum. Current formal conditions still require verification.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Public Administration and Organisation Science degree studies how governments and public organisations make decisions, deliver services and respond to social problems. Students study policy, law and management and conduct research in organisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The listed courses and profiling space account for 180 EC. Utrecht’s progression rules and the conditions on elective study still need verification before a complete comparison can be shown.

componentNotes.bo-y2-choice: This 7.5 EC elective is part of the 37.5 EC profiling space.
componentNotes.bo-y2-qualitative: Students use interviews and observations to investigate a question from an organisation.
componentNotes.bo-y3-profiling: Four 7.5 EC electives. Options include individual courses, a minor, study abroad or an internship, subject to Utrecht’s rules.
componentNotes.bo-y3-capstone: Students analyse a public issue and write an advisory report.
componentNotes.bo-y3-thesis: Students prepare an individual research project in period three and carry it out and write the thesis in period four.
